episodes.title: The Lownie Report: Nick Bryant on Epstein’s Black Book and Decades of Blackmail in US Politics
episodes.description:
Originally recorded on 17 August 2026.
Early access for channel members. This episode goes public on Saturday 14 November.

Subscribe to The Lownie Report on Substack: https://andrewlownie.substack.com

Order the newly updated paperback of 'Entitled: The Rise and Fall of the House of York' here: https://link.amazon/B09Y4WKNe

It was my pleasure to welcome Nick Bryant onto the Lownie Report Podcast for a wide-ranging, fascinating and somewhat harrowing deep dive into his investigative work into abuses of power and cover-ups in the USA. Nick has been a pioneer in uncovering some of America’s darkest scandals, beginning with the Franklin scandal and now with the Epstein scandal.

Nick was the first to obtain the infamous black book and the Epstein flight logs and has experienced huge challenges in his pursuit of the truth. His investigation into Franklin alone took seven years and, he says, brought death threats, harassment, professional isolation and considerable personal cost.

Nick explains how his investigation of the Franklin scandal led him to recognise what he believes were striking parallels with Jeffrey Epstein: networks involving vulnerable young people, powerful figures, blackmail and deliberate failures by law enforcement and the judicial system.

He argues that the Epstein story cannot be understood simply as the crimes of Epstein and Ghislaine Maxwell, but as a much wider system of facilitators and powerful interests which has never been properly investigated, despite countless employees such as limo drivers, pilots and assistants who could easily be compelled to talk to the authorities.

Nick told me the remarkable story of obtaining Epstein’s black book, tracking down victims whose details appeared within it, and discovering evidence that had stark echoes of his previous research. We talked about what we can infer from what some see as the Rosetta stone of the Epstein story.

After initially struggling to interest the American media, he eventually published the black book and flight logs with Gawker in 2015, after which, he says, the floodgates finally opened.

We talked about his belief that intelligence agencies and political interests played, and continue to play, a role in protecting Epstein; the extraordinary 2008 plea deal and immunity granted to his alleged co-conspirators; the reluctance of the media and authorities to pursue leads; and why Bryant believes survivors have been left without adequate protection, making it harder for them to come forward against rich and powerful figures.

We also covered the role of lawyers acting for Epstein’s victims, including questions about settlements, releases and the extent to which legal representatives had conflicts of interest or connections that deserved greater scrutiny.

As Nick said, the Epstein scandal has been a bipartisan cover-up spanning four presidents and almost twenty years and it was only the full force of Trump’s MAGA base that finally forced the partial release of the Epstein files, albeit in a manner that has ended up obscuring the President’s role in this story and with millions of records still unreleased or already destroyed.

episodes.title: Could Andrew be Charged as Soon as Next Year?
episodes.description:
Subscribe to The Lownie Report on Substack: https://andrewlownie.substack.com

Order the newly updated paperback of 'Entitled: The Rise and Fall of the House of York' here: https://link.amazon/B09Y4WKNe

I’m delighted to share this week’s Lownie Report Podcast, where we look at Police Scotland’s interest in Balmoral, Andrew’s summons to give evidence in the Selman Turk case, the claims surrounding Thomas Markle and the King’s Caribbean tour.

We begin in Scotland. I explain how the story of Police Scotland’s inquiry came to light, why Scotland had been missing from the list of forces looking at Andrew, and what I heard during my research about women being brought to Balmoral and the lodges on the estate.

I also discuss the gagging orders that have kept people silent, why so many are still frightened of speaking out, and why my police sources believe their investigation now has real momentum and that it’s possible we may see charges as early as next year.

We then turn to the High Court. Andrew has been summoned to give evidence in the case brought by Nebahat Isbilen against Selman Turk, the first time a member of the Royal Family has been summoned to appear in court since the 19th century. We go through the payments that reached the Yorks, including the £750,000 paid to Andrew, the £225,000 to Sarah Ferguson and the money that landed in Eugenie’s account, along with the many explanations the family have given for them. We also discuss Pitch@Palace, Alphabet Capital, Tarek Kaituni and Andrew’s activities in Libya, an area I hope to write about more fully, and what the trial might finally reveal about his finances.

We also look at the troubling reports about Thomas Markle that have emerged in the press, the letter of concern said to have been sent to the Metropolitan Police, what Meghan was told about it and how that fits with the timeline of her estrangement from her father.

I discussed too the huge pressures that Royal protection officers are under to keep quiet and the subtle and not so subtle ways that they can be pressured, including the carrot of honours and the stick of using bureaucracy to make their job untenable or moving them to a much less cushy position.

Finally, we turn to the King’s tour of the Caribbean, the debate over reparations and an apology, and how the government’s mixed messages in the days before his speech left him unnecessarily exposed and revealed a Foreign Office not operating at its best.

I also give my view on where the reign stands four years in, and the sense of drift I see at the top of the monarchy with a King who has his mother’s habit of sticking his head in the sand but seemingly hasn’t inherited the ruthlessness that Queen Elizabeth II was capable of when the crown required it, for example when she rejected out of hand Harry and Meghan’s half-in/half-out proposal.

episodes.title: The Lownie Report Podcast: Has Sarah Ferguson Done a Deal?
episodes.description: It's been a busy week for royal news and this week's Lownie Report Podcast looks at the return of Sarah Ferguson and the extent to which it has been planned with precision by the former Duchess to coincide with the Sussex circus and the growing disquiet around a King who increasingly seems unable or unwilling to keep his family under control. The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. I discuss why I think it's likely that Sarah Ferguson has done a deal that ensures she will not face charges and why this could spell very bad news for Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor. I also covered Fergie's relationship with her daughters and sons-in-law and why the 'tripod', as she calls herself, Beatrice and Eugenie, have all distanced themselves from Andrew, mainly to try and preserve their own business sidelines and so the York sisters can hang on to their lucrative royal titles. It may also be that the daughters genuinely are disgusted by their father's alleged actions. As I pointed out though, Fergie can hardly claim to have the same distaste given her deep friendship with Epstein and her associations with convicted paedophile Peter Nygard and the now-jailed P Diddy. Relationships that run counter to the reputation she cultivated as a champion of trafficked women. I also covered the news that an alleged victim of Andrew, who was trafficked to Royal Lodge and then given a tour of Buckingham Palace, is now considering talking to the police. This is encouraging news and may help inspire other victims to come forward. However, briefing that the investigation into Mandelson may be about to be dropped due to insufficient evidence and a lack of cooperation from the US Justice Department is less encouraging. Especially given how clear-cut and damning the evidence already in the public domain seems to be. We also discussed what may be about to be revealed in the upcoming unsealing of the libel case between Virginia Giuffre and Ghislaine Maxwell, which I believe could be highly significant for both Andrew and Sarah Ferguson. Finally we looked at the revelations about King Charles in the Sunday Times this week and why the King increasingly looks weak in his handling of the Yorks and the Sussexes and to be captain of a ship that is beginning to look rudderless. The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. To hear more, visit andrewlownie.substack.com

episodes.title: 'There’s a Sort of Giant Cover-up That’s Not Just the Palace, it’s Actually the Government Itself'
episodes.description: I enjoyed my discussion with Sonia Poulton, who has followed my work on Andrew and the Yorks from the early stages. We discussed how the publication of Entitled: The Rise and Fall of the House of York, the Epstein files and Virginia Giuffre’s story helped create a tipping point in public understanding of Andrew’s behaviour and the wider questions it raises about how Andrew was allowed to act with impunity for so long. The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. We also talked about the financial revelations at the heart of the book, including Andrew’s time as trade envoy, the role of wealthy friends and backers who accompanied him on taxpayer-funded trips, and the extraordinary difficulty of obtaining information that should, in my view, be in the public domain. As I said to Sonia, I’ve filed hundreds of Freedom of Information requests and not a single one has answered the questions that I asked. Finally, we looked at the police investigations, the need for a proper parliamentary inquiry, and the growing pressure for greater transparency around the Royal Family’s finances and business interests, pressure that is finally having an effect on the King and Prince William, who are at least moving in the right direction with the upcoming release of their tax returns. episodes.title: The Lownie Report: The Campaign to Discredit Epstein's Victims
episodes.description:
An incredible episode of The Lownie Report this week with Anne Cheever, who has done some brilliant work over the past few years investigating the network of people surrounding the Yorks and Ghislaine Maxwell who have used a multitude of techniques to try and discredit the brave victims who have come forward and spoken publicly about their abuse. 

Anne has called this network the ‘She-Wolves’ and I highly recommend her series on Substack which looks at how figures like Fergie, Victoria Hervey and George Bing Tonks have played a significant role in muddying the waters, for example with the ridiculous notion that the now infamous photo of the late Virginia Giuffre was fake or that the victims were not telling the truth.

We discussed parallels with the Amber Heard trial, how bots are used en-masse across social media to spread misinformation - I have experienced the latter myself - and how Dropbox has been used as a repository for files that help make this campaign of hate possible and highly organised. 

We also discussed Maria Farmer, one of Epstein's earliest known victims and a woman of extraordinary courage, who has had to endure not only the trauma of her abuse but the very deliberate infiltration of her inner circle by bad actors secretly recording her private conversations in order to sabotage her legal case against the FBI. 

Anne also makes a compelling case that the ultimate goal of this whole network is to secure a presidential pardon for Ghislaine Maxwell, who is already receiving what can only be described as extraordinarily preferential treatment in prison; private computer access, her mail handled personally by the warden, conditions that frankly sound less like a federal penitentiary and more like a rather inconvenient hotel. The message being sent could not be clearer and it is a deeply troubling one for anyone who cares about justice for the survivors.

Both Anne and I have come up against disgusting behaviour and allegations since trying to shine a light on the Epstein saga and I salute her tenacity and bravery in carrying on the quest for truth despite such powerful opposition and abuse. I can’t recommend her Substack enough and I hope you will enjoy this insightful interview that is as riveting as it is horrifying.

episodes.title: The Lownie Report Podcast: Mixed Messages from Police Investigating Andrew & When I Met Fergie to Discuss 'Entitled'
episodes.description: We discuss the latest developments regarding Andrew and Fergie and also cover some pertinent parallels taking us back, via Mountbatten, to the Cambridge Spy Ring and how I first learnt about the British establishment’s cover-up playbook while writing Stalin’s Englishman: The Lives of Guy Burgess . The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. We cover a fascinating 1997 TV interview with Sarah Ferguson that has recently been uploaded to YouTube by Ruby Wax. It was recorded when some of her biggest early scandals were only just in the rear-view mirror. Wax’s inimitable interview technique is highly effective in revealing as much about Ferguson’s modus operandi post-scandal as the multitude of reasons she gives for her mistakes. She claims ignorance and naivety in her consistent attraction to the wrong men and bad decisions, refers to the solace of the words of St Francis of Assisi, compares herself to Morgan Freeman’s character in Shawshank Redemption and doesn’t demur when Wax generously posits that she’s actually more of a Robin Hood figure, since she donated some of her £5m Coutts overdraft to charity. As I wrote in Entitled , the former Duchess would wheel out exactly the same excuses after the scandals that peppered the following three decades of her career, ostensibly outside the Royal Family but very much operating within its protection via her ex-husband. I also discuss my meeting with Sarah Ferguson when I began work on my book back in 2022. She had all the charisma you might expect and brought her recent Mills & Boon book and some Ginger & Moss products as a gift, and initially seemed co-operative. Discussions with her team carried on for a few weeks before interviewees began to drop out and letters from lawyers began to drop in through the letterbox. The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support my work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. The conversation also looks at the mixed messages coming out of the police investigation, with briefing that seems contradictory at times, and how there seems a distinct possibility that if no charges are brought, the public will be told the matter is closed as far as the Crown and the government are concerned. We also looked at what effect this has actually had on the Royal Family and whether anything substantial has changed in respect of public accountability and transparency. I quoted Harold Macmillan’s line: “When my gamekeeper shoots a fox, he doesn’t go and hang it up outside the Master of Foxhounds’ drawing room; he buries it out of sight.” An apt metaphor and an attitude that still seemed apparent in the way the establishment covered up for Andrew until Virginia Giuffre and the Epstein Files forced them into action. An example of the “Jolly Good Chaps” theory of history, which has a habit of protecting men who are quite the opposite. The Lownie Report is a reader-supported publication.
